claim: LLM-generated paper reviews are uniformly positive and fail to discriminate paper quality: GPT-4/Claude-Opus/Gemini-1.5 gave average scores of 7.43 to accepted and 7.47 to rejected NLP papers (humans 6.41 vs 4.81), praised the writing of every paper, and produced more expert-flagged deficient segments than human reviewers (13.97% vs 6.27%), largely out-of-scope or paper-unspecific critiques.

paper.title: LLMs Assist NLP Researchers: Critique Paper (Meta-)Reviewing
paper.citation_source: Semantic Scholar Graph API POST https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/batch?fields=title,citationCount,publicationDate,externalIds,venue (id arXiv:2406.16253)
paper.s2_batch_record_title: LLMs Assist NLP Researchers: Critique Paper (Meta-)Reviewing

experiment.location_in_paper: Section 3 (ReviewCritique, Table 1), Section 4.1 (Table 3 error types; 'Strengths', 'Weaknesses', 'Writing', 'Recommendation Score' paragraphs; Figure 1 ITF-IDF), Section 4.2 (LLMs as meta-reviewers)
experiment.task_or_benchmark: ReviewCritique: 100 NLP papers submitted to ICLR/NeurIPS 2020-2023 with 380 human reviews; 20-paper subset (10 accepted/10 rejected) with 60 LLM reviews (3 per LLM); expert sentence-level 'Deficient' labels.
experiment.intervention_or_prompts: Prompt with ICLR review guidelines, random example human reviews (accepted and rejected), ICLR 2024 template; LLM also outputs a 1-10 recommendation score (Table 14 prompt).
experiment.evaluation_procedure: NLP experts (PhD/AC experience) annotate each review segment as Deficient with explanation and 23 error types; compare rates; ITF-IDF specificity metric and BERTScore inter-LLM similarity; recommendation scores vs acceptance.
experiment.metric: % deficient reviews/segments; mean score by decision; ITF-IDF
experiment.main_comparison: LLM-generated vs human-written reviews of the same papers
experiment.main_result: Deficient segments 13.97% (LLM) vs 6.27% (human); 100% of LLM reviews vs 71.57% of human reviews contain a deficient segment. Mean LLM score 7.43 (accepted) vs 7.47 (rejected); human 6.41 vs 4.81. 53.2% of LLM 'strength' segments rephrase the submission; LLMs praised writing for all papers incl. the 15% humans agreed were unclear. Top LLM error 'Out-of-scope' 30.49% of deficient segments. ITF-IDF specificity human 6.04 vs Claude Opus 4.09, Gemini 3.82, GPT-4 3.34.

downstream.title: Prompt Injection Attacks on LLM Generated Reviews of Scientific Publications
downstream.summary: On 1,000 ICLR 2024 papers, LLM reviews are biased toward acceptance (>95% accept in many models) even without injection (abstract read).

downstream.title: Are We There Yet?
downstream.summary: GPT-4o-based reviews map to borderline ~5.3 ratings with similar tone regardless of paper quality; incomplete papers rated near full-paper level.

downstream.title: LLM-REVal: Can We Trust LLM Reviewers Yet?
downstream.summary: LLM reviewers systematically rate LLM-authored papers above human papers and misjudge some human papers, diverging from human reviewers.

downstream.title: The AI Scientist
downstream.summary: Counterpoint: an engineered GPT-4o reviewer (reflection, few-shot, ensembling) reportedly reaches near-human balanced accuracy on ICLR 2022 accept/reject (numbers not verifiable from the truncated paperclip text; abstract only).

downstream_summary: Score inflation / acceptance bias of off-the-shelf LLM reviewers is reproduced at larger scale with 2025 models; carefully engineered reviewer pipelines can be better calibrated, so the effect is prompt/pipeline dependent.
notability_notes: EMNLP 2024; 87 S2 citations; the ReviewCritique dataset is a standard resource for LLM-review quality.
gaps: Only 20 papers (60 LLM reviews) for the score comparison; score difference not significance-tested in the text read. AI Scientist reviewer numbers not verified (paperclip text truncated to 5 KB).
